title: A Decade of International Energy III: Rules of Order in Regulation, Disorderly Opportunism, and the Looming Disorder of AI Electricity Demand
content: This is my third and final review of a decade of contributions to International Energy—particularly how I regularly return to specific themes illustrating the extent to which regulation works to promote energy services the public wants at reasonable cost. In my July 2025 column,1 I revisited five themes, particularly the challenge of controlling industry and managing social costs when energy regulation breaks down. Good regulatory institutions are challenging to establish—but the benefits are substantial when they succeed. In September 2025,2 I concentrated on the limits of regulatory control—and the advantages to consumers and businesses when new technologies and useful competitors emerge on the other side of regulatory boundaries. Strong limits on regulatory authority are vital in this respect.
author: Jeff D. Makholm
